facts.fact: The handbook says the Eswatini DroughtMap Hub, run with the National Drought Management Center, Ministry of Agriculture and Meteorological Service, computes a Combined Drought Indicator from CHIRPS and MODIS satellite data and publishes it per inkhundla in a public area.
The handbook says the Combined Drought Indicator is computed automatically each month for the previous month, then reviewed, validated and published.

facts.fact: An RCMRD report for Eswatini's National Disaster Management Agency (CTCN-funded) says crop monitoring pilots combining drones and Sentinel-2 imagery were run at four sites in April 2021, and a satellite-based maize yield model was applied nationally for 2020.
facts.system: NDMA UAV and satellite crop monitoring pilot

facts.fact: The Swaziland Meteorological Service's Agrometeorological Unit issued its agromet bulletin for 21-31 October 2024, assessing vegetation condition with FAO-GIEWS NDVI anomaly and Vegetation Health Index imagery.
The Agrometeorological Unit's bulletin is issued per dekad, Issue 03 of season 2024/25 released 4 November 2024 for 21-31 October 2024.
FEWS NET's October 2026 Southern Africa seasonal monitor reports well-above-average NDVI vegetation and above-average soil moisture in Eswatini.
